newsitem.title: UK: Reuters up after New York briefings.
newsitem.headline: Reuters up after New York briefings.

text.p: Shares in Reuters Holdings Plc rose on Thursday, after upbeat analyst comment following a series of presentations by company executives to analysts and fund managers in New York, dealers said.
Extending a rebound from its 16-month low of 573p set on April 14, the stock was up 16-1/2p at 651 by 0940 GMT, in volume of 4.31 million shares.

Analysts at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett, joint broker to the news and financial information company, repeated a positive view on Reuters shares and highlighted growth being generated by its latest 3000 range of information products.

Hoare Govett said Reuters was on track to reach its target for 3000 product sales and said some 14 percent of sales of the product were being made to new customers, suggesting that it was helping increase market share.

The brokerage added that there had been an encouraging pickup in sales of the foreign exchange transaction product Dealing 2002 in the first quarter of the year -- contrasting with quiet trading conditions in forex in second half of 1996.
Analysts at Hoare Govett said that, while reported growth in Reuters 1997 profits would be hit by strength of sterling, this did not imply a long-term impact on the underlying business.
"It isn't something that will affect the long term secular growth profile or its cash generation," one said.

Reuters warned last month that the strong pound had cut first quarter revenues by two percent to 699 million stg and said that if sterling remained at its current levels, it expected little or no growth in headline pre-tax profit at the half-year stage.
However, it said there was an underlying growth of eight percent in first-quarter revenues from a year earlier.

A spokeswoman for Reuters said chief executive Peter Job and other company executives on Wednesday had briefed U.S. analysts on progress with the 3000 range, transaction products, the Instinet share dealing service and other Reuters operations.
